scope: Post-publication full-timeline human review of the v59 H3 shadow and residual-hand cleanup
summary: The v59 promotion is withdrawn: denser full-timeline review finds recognizable source-human hands and forearms in multiple intervals, including a large horizontal forearm near frame 462.
evidence: review/frame462-lower-right-v59.png shows a clear peach human forearm extending from the generated robot/flower contact region across the lower-right work area.

review/v59-timeline-1.jpg through review/v59-timeline-4.jpg expose additional residual-human hand/forearm intervals around frames 135--240 and 405--474 that the earlier sparse review did not sample densely enough.

review/lower-roi-skin-components-440-520.jpg shows that the global connected-component selector merges the forearm with flower/table-coloured pixels and then rejects it under the 15,000-pixel maximum-area gate.
No replacement showcase is published from this audit.
lessons: Sparse early/late frame sampling is insufficient for a 660-frame human-removal claim; all interaction phases need dense timeline coverage.
Connected components must be formed after a task-specific spatial crop or tracked negative matte because global skin-colour connectivity can merge a real forearm with flowers and table content.
Neutral shadow attenuation and recognizable human-limb removal require independent masks, strengths, and acceptance checks.
limitations: The audit identifies the failure intervals but does not itself provide an accepted corrected video.
The source pose-arm track is spatially misaligned with the generated residual arm near frame 462 and cannot be used as a direct deletion matte.
next_actions: Use densely reviewed, temporally interpolated residual-arm keyframes for the strong negative matte while keeping robot metal and verified flower pixels on top.
Increase only the neutral-shadow spatial reach while reducing its blend strength, then rerun all 660-frame locality, temporal, dense-review, and decode gates.
